prompt: Given the head of a linked list, decide whether it contains a cycle using O(1) extra memory.
why: Floyd's tortoise and hare: a fast pointer laps the slow one only if there's a cycle.
trap: A visited set works but costs O(n) memory.

prompt: Return the middle node of a singly linked list in one pass.
why: Fast moves two steps, slow one. When fast hits the end, slow is in the middle.
trap: Binary search needs random access; a linked list doesn't have it.

prompt: Repeatedly replace a number by the sum of the squares of its digits. Decide whether it reaches 1 or loops forever.
why: The sequence is an implicit linked list. Run a fast and a slow walker; they meet in a loop or at 1.
trap: No list in sight, but any "next state" function is one.

prompt: An array of n+1 integers holds values from 1 to n, so one repeats. Find it without modifying the array and in constant space.
why: Treat i → nums[i] as a linked list. The duplicate is where the cycle begins: Floyd finds it.
trap: Binary search on value counts also works, but in O(n log n).

prompt: A linked list may loop back on itself. Return the node where the cycle begins, or null.
why: After fast and slow meet, restart one at the head; moving both one step at a time, they meet at the cycle's start.
trap: Union-find detects cycles in graphs you build, not in a list you walk.
